01System Design 101 · S19 · Guide 1 / 8

5 Functions to Merge Data with Pandas

Excel ke bina data kaise merge karein? Pandas ke 5 functions hain: Concat, Append, Merge, Join, Combine. Har ek ka apna kaam hai — shards jodna, crawler ka data add karna, keys par join karna, ya clean karte waqt values chunna. Code ke saath samjho.

1. Data merge karna — do register jodna

Do register hain: ek me naam aur sheher, dusre me naam aur salary. Dono ko ek register banana hai — naam ke hisaab se jodna hai. Yehi merge hai.

kabhi register upar-neeche jodne hote hain (concat), kabhi naye page chipkane hote hain (append), kabhi dono register se chhoti value chunni hoti hai (combine). Pandas ke 5 functions — 5 alag tareeke.

2. 5 functions — ek-ek karke

Guide ke hisaab se — har function kya karta hai, aur production me kahan use hota hai.

Concat — upar-neeche ya side-by-side jodo

pd.concat() — do tables ko vertical ya horizontal combine karta hai. Vertical matlab ek ke neeche dusri, horizontal matlab side-by-side.

Use case: data shards se aata hai — jaise har din ka data alag file me hai — to concat se sabko ek table banao. Production data analysis me sabse zyada use hone wala function hai.

pd.concat([df_jan, df_feb])  # upar-neeche
pd.concat([df1, df2], axis=1)  # side-by-side

Append — naye rows jodo

df.append() — existing table me naye rows add karta hai. (Naye pandas me concat hi use hota hai, lekin concept wahi hai.)

Use case: web crawler — naya data crawl hote hi use purani table me append kar do. Har crawl ke baad table badhti jati hai.

df = df.append(new_rows)
# ya naye pandas me:
df = pd.concat([df, new_rows])

Merge — keys par join karo (SQL join jaisa)

pd.merge() — do tables ko keys par horizontally jodta hai — bilkul database joins ki tarah (inner, left, right, outer).

Use case: alag domains ka data jodna — jaise users table aur orders table, user_id key par. Dono me same key ho to merge karo.

pd.merge(users, orders, on='user_id', how='left')

Join — index par outer join

df.join() — merge jaisa hi hai, lekin index par kaam karta hai aur database ke outer joins jaisa behave karta hai.

Use case: jab dono tables ka index hi key ho — jaise date index par do time-series jodni hon. Merge se zyada convenient hota hai index-based kaam me.

df1.join(df2)  # index par join
Merge vs Join: Merge columns (keys) par, Join index par. Dono hi SQL joins jaisi cheez hain — bas key kahan hai, ye farak hai.

Combine — calculate kar ke jodo

df.combine() — do tables jodte waqt calculation apply karta hai. Example: dono tables me same cell ho to chhoti value chun lo.

Use case: data cleansing — do sources se data aaya ho aur tumhe best value chunni ho (jaise minimum price, ya latest value).

df1.combine(df2, np.minimum)  # har cell me chhoti value

3. Kaun sa function, kab?

FunctionKya karta haiKab use karo
ConcatVertical / horizontal combineShards ya alag files ka data jodna
AppendExisting table me rows addCrawler ka naya data add karna
MergeKeys par join (SQL jaisa)Alag domains ka data, same key par
JoinIndex par outer joinIndex hi key ho (time-series)
CombineCalculation ke saath combineData cleansing — best value chunni ho
import pandas as pd
# Shards jodna
all_data = pd.concat([df1, df2, df3])
# Users + Orders
full = pd.merge(users, orders, on='user_id', how='left')
# Do prices me se chhoti chunna
best = df_a.combine(df_b, min)

4. Try karo — data merge karo

Neeche steps me dekho har function ek hi example data par kya karta hai.

  1. 1. Concat — shards jodo
    [Data] Jan: 100 rows, Feb: 120 rows — alag files
    [pd.concat] Dono ko upar-neeche joda
    [Result] 220 rows — ek table taiyaar
  2. 2. Append — crawler data
    [Crawler] 15 naye rows mile
    [append] Purani table me add kiye
    [Result] 220 → 235 rows
  3. 3. Merge — users + orders
    [Users] user_id, name — 50 rows
    [Orders] user_id, amount — 80 rows
    [pd.merge on='user_id'] Dono jode — 80 rows, naam + amount ek saath
  4. 4. Combine — best price chuno
    [Source A] Price ₹499, [Source B] Price ₹449
    [combine + min] Chhoti value chuni: ₹449
    [Result] Data clean — customer ko best price dikhega

5. Functions — ek table me

FunctionDirectionSQL jaisa kya
ConcatVertical / horizontalUNION jaisa (vertical)
AppendRows add karnaINSERT jaisa
MergeKeys par horizontalJOIN (inner/left/right/outer)
JoinIndex parOuter join
CombineCalculation ke saathCASE WHEN jaisa — value chunna

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Merge aur Join ko ek samajhna — Merge columns par, Join index par hota hai.
2. Concat me axis bhoolna — axis=0 vertical, axis=1 horizontal; galat axis se shape bigad jayegi.
3. Merge me ‘how’ na batana — default inner hai; left join chahiye tha to data kho jayega.
4. Append ko loop me chalana — har append poori table copy karta hai; pehle list banao, phir ek concat karo.
5. Combine ko sirf ‘merge’ samajhna — combine me calculation hoti hai (min/max), sirf jodna nahi.

7. Interview corner

Q: “Concat aur Merge me kya farak hai?”
A: Concat tables ko upar-neeche ya side-by-side jodta hai bina keys ke — jaise shards jodna. Merge keys par join karta hai, SQL joins ki tarah — jaise users aur orders ko user_id par jodna.
Q: “Append loop me kyun nahi chalana chahiye?”
A: Kyunki har append poori table ko copy karke nayi table banata hai — loop me ye O(n²) ho jata hai. Pehle saare chunks list me rakho, phir ek baar concat karo.
Q: “Combine kab use karte hain?”
A: Jab do tables jodte waqt calculation karni ho — jaise dono me same cell ho to chhoti value chunni ho. Ye data cleansing me kaam aata hai.

8. Quick check

1. Do tables ko keys par SQL join ki tarah jodne ke liye kaun sa function hai?

  • ✓ Merge — on='user_id' jaise keys par
  • Concat
  • Combine

2. Web crawler ka naya data purani table me add karne ke liye kya use karte hain?

  • ✓ Append (ya concat) — naye rows jodna
  • Join
  • Combine
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Concat (shards jodna), Append (naye rows), Merge (keys par SQL join), Join (index par), Combine (calculation ke saath — cleansing). Kaam ke hisaab se function chuno — har merge ek jaisa nahi hota.

02System Design 101 · S19 · Guide 2 / 8

Key Data Terms

Data Warehouse, Data Lake, Data Mart, Delta Lake, Data Pipeline — ye terms har jagah sunne ko milte hain, lekin farak kya hai? Ye page data ke key terms ko ek-ek karke, example ke saath samjhata hai — taaki interview me kabhi confuse na ho.

1. Data terms — kitchen ke bartan wali kahani

Kitchen me: godown (sab kuch raw rakha hai), fridge (saja hua, turant use hone wala), aur dabba (ek khaas cheez ke liye chhota sa hissa). Data ki duniya me bhi wahi hai: Lake (godown), Warehouse (fridge), Mart (dabba).

Terms confuse isliye hote hain kyunki sab “data store” lagte hain — lekin har ek ka kaam, structure aur user alag hai.

2. Key terms — 5 tabs me

Guide ke hisaab se — har term kya hai, aur kab use hota hai.

Data Warehouse — saja hua, structured store

Ek bada, structured repository — alag-alag sources se integrated data, complex querying aur historical analysis ke liye. Data yahan aane se pehle clean aur organize hota hai (schema-on-write).

Example: company ka saal bhar ka sales data — “pichhle 5 saal me kaun se sheher me kya bika?” — aisi queries warehouse par chalti hain. Tools: Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift.

Data Mart — warehouse ka chhota hissa

Warehouse ka focused, department-specific subset — jaise sirf Sales team ka data. Chhota hota hai, isliye queries tez chalti hain aur team ko sirf apna data dikhta hai.

Example: Sales mart — sirf sales ka data, marketing team ko isse matlab nahi. Mart warehouse se banta hai, alag se nahi.

Data Lake — raw data ka godown

Ek vishal pool — raw, unstructured data apne native format me store hota hai, jab tak zaroorat na ho. Structure tab lagta hai jab data padha jata hai (schema-on-read).

Example: logs, images, videos, clickstream — sab lake me daal do, baad me decide karo kya kaam ka hai. Tools: S3, ADLS. Lake sasta hai, lekin bina governance ke “data swamp” ban jata hai.

Delta Lake — lake par reliability

Ek open-source storage layer jo data lakes par reliability aur ACID transactions laata hai — batch aur streaming dono ko ek saath chalata hai.

Fayda: lake ka flexibility + warehouse ki reliability. Data lakehouse ka concept yahin se aata hai — lake aur warehouse ka mix.

Data Pipeline — data ko le jaane wala rasta

Data Pipeline ek process hai jo data ko ek jagah se dusri jagah le jata hai — collect, clean, transform, load. Pipeline ke bina warehouse aur lake me data aata hi nahi.

Data Lakehouse — lake + warehouse ka combination: lake ki cheap storage, warehouse ki querying aur ACID. Aaj ki modern architecture aksar lakehouse hoti hai.

Interview line: “Lake = raw aur sasta, Warehouse = structured aur tez, Mart = department ka hissa, Lakehouse = dono ka mix.”

Data Mesh — data ki ownership domain teams ke paas

Data Mesh ek architectural aur organizational approach hai — data ki ownership aur delivery ek central data team ke paas nahi, domain-specific, cross-functional teams ke paas hoti hai. Har team apne domain ka data khud own karti hai aur use ek product ki tarah treat karti hai.

Example: badi company me Sales team apna sales data khud manage kare, Marketing apna — central team sirf platform aur standards de. Ye Data Lakehouse se alag hai: Lakehouse ek technology hai, Mesh ek organizational tareeka hai.

3. Lake vs Warehouse — ek table me

CheezData LakeData Warehouse
DataRaw, unstructured, native formatStructured, cleaned, organized
SchemaSchema-on-read (padhte waqt)Schema-on-write (likhte waqt)
CostSasta (object storage)Mehenga (compute + storage)
UsersData scientists, ML engineersAnalysts, BI, business users
QueriesExploratory, ML trainingReports, dashboards, historical analysis

Yaad rakhne ka tareeka: Lake me sab kuch daal do (raw), Warehouse me sirf kaam ka, saja hua data (structured), Mart me ek team ka hissa.

4. Try karo — ek click ka data, lake se dashboard tak

Neeche steps me dekho ek user ke click ka data lake se lekar dashboard tak kaise jata hai.

  1. 1. Click hua
    [User] Website par 'Buy' dabaya
    [Pipeline] Click event collect hua — raw JSON
    [Lake] Raw event S3 lake me gaya — native format me
  2. 2. Clean + Load
    [Pipeline] Data clean hua — galat entries hatayi
    [Warehouse] Structured data Snowflake me load hua
    [Delta Lake] ACID guarantee — aadha data load nahi hoga
  3. 3. Mart + Dashboard
    [Mart] Sales team ka mart update hua
    [Dashboard] 'Aaj ki sales: ₹12 lakh' — 2 second me
    [ML] Lake se raw data le kar recommendation model train hua

5. Terms — ek table me

TermEk line meExample tool
Data WarehouseStructured, historical analysisSnowflake, BigQuery, Redshift
Data MartWarehouse ka department subsetSales mart, Marketing mart
Data LakeRaw data ka pool, schema-on-readS3, ADLS
Delta LakeLake par ACID + reliabilityDelta Lake (open-source)
Data PipelineData ko le jaane wala processAirflow, Spark
Data LakehouseLake + Warehouse ka mixDatabricks, Snowflake
Data MeshData ownership domain teams ke paasDomain teams, data-as-a-product

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Lake aur Warehouse ko ek samajhna — lake raw hai, warehouse structured; kaam alag hai.
2. Lake me bina governance ke data daalna — ‘data swamp’ ban jata hai, kuch dhoondhna namumkin.
3. Har query warehouse par chalana — exploratory/ML kaam lake par, reports warehouse par.
4. Mart ko alag database samajhna — mart warehouse ka subset hai, alag source nahi.
5. Pipeline ko ‘sirf ETL’ samajhna — pipeline me collect, clean, transform, load aur monitoring — sab aata hai.

7. Interview corner

Q: “Data Lake aur Data Warehouse me kya farak hai?”
A: Lake me raw, unstructured data native format me store hota hai (schema-on-read) — sasta aur flexible. Warehouse me data clean aur structured hota hai (schema-on-write) — tez queries aur reports ke liye. Lake data scientists ke liye, warehouse analysts ke liye.
Q: “Data Mart kya hai?”
A: Warehouse ka department-specific subset — jaise sirf Sales ka data. Chhota hota hai, queries tez hoti hain, aur team ko sirf apna data dikhta hai.
Q: “Delta Lake kya karta hai?”
A: Ye data lakes par reliability aur ACID transactions laata hai — lake ki flexibility + warehouse ki reliability. Isi se lakehouse architecture banti hai.

8. Quick check

1. Raw, unstructured data native format me kahan store hota hai?

  • ✓ Data Lake me — schema-on-read
  • Data Warehouse me
  • Data Mart me

2. Sales team ko sirf apna data chahiye — kya use karenge?

  • ✓ Data Mart — warehouse ka department-specific subset
  • Poora Data Lake
  • Delta Lake
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Lake = raw godown (sasta, schema-on-read), Warehouse = saja hua store (structured, reports), Mart = ek team ka hissa, Delta Lake = lake par ACID, Pipeline = data ka rasta. Har term ka kaam alag hai — naam se confuse mat ho.

03System Design 101 · S19 · Guide 3 / 8

ChatGPT Timeline

ChatGPT achanak nahi aaya — uske peeche 70 saal ki research hai. 1950s ke rule-based models se lekar 2017 ke Transformer aur 2018 ke baad ke bade models tak — ye timeline batata hai hum yahan tak kaise pahunche.

1. ChatGPT ki kahani — ek ped ki kahani

Ek bada ped ek din me nahi ugta — pehle beej (1950s rules), phir chhota paudha (1980s ML), phir tehniyaan (1990s neural networks), phir mazboot trunk (2017 Transformer), aur phir phal (ChatGPT).

Har decade ne agle decade ki neev rakhi. Transformer ke bina ChatGPT nahi hota, aur neural networks ke bina Transformer nahi hota.

2. Timeline — 5 eras

Guide ke hisaab se — har era me kya hua.

1950s — Rule-based models

Is stage me log primitive, rule-based models use karte the — “agar ye to wo” jaise haath se likhe gaye rules. Machine ko har cheez rule se batani padti thi.

Limit: duniya ke har rule ko likhna namumkin hai — isliye ye models sirf bahut simple kaam kar sakte the.

1980s — Machine Learning shuru

1980s se machine learning pick up karne laga — classification jaise kaam ke liye. Training chhote data par hoti thi.

Ab machine rules nahi, data se seekhne lagi — lekin data aur compute dono kam the, isliye models chhote the.

1990s–2000s — Neural Networks

Neural networks ne human brain ko imitate karna shuru kiya — labeling aur training ke liye. 3 main types:

CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) — visual tasks (images) ke liye. RNN (Recurrent Neural Network) — natural language tasks ke liye. GAN (Generative Adversarial Network) — do networks (generative + discriminative) se nayi images banana — generative model jo asli jaisi nayi cheezein bana sakta hai.

2017 — “Attention Is All You Need”

2017 me aaya paper “Attention Is All You Need” — isne Transformer model diya, jo generative AI ki neev hai. Transformer ne parallelism se training time bahut kam kar diya — pehle ke models (RNN) ek ke baad ek chalte the, Transformer ek saath chalta hai.

Attention ka matlab: model khud decide karta hai sentence me kis word par dhyan dena hai. Yehi wajah hai Transformer itna powerful hai.

Interview line: “Transformer se pehle AI slow thi, Transformer ke baad scale hui — parallelism ne training time ko hafton se dinon me la diya.”

2018–Now — Bade models aur ChatGPT

Transformer ki progress se massive data par train hue models aaye. Human demonstration learning content bani — insaan kaise likhta hai, model wahi seekhta hai.

Ab AI writers articles, news, technical docs aur code bhi likh sakte hain — iski commercial value bahut badi hai, aur isne duniya bhar me whirlwind macha di hai. ChatGPT iska sabse famous example hai.

3. Timeline — ek nazar me

EraKya huaLimit / Breakthrough
1950sRule-based modelsHar rule haath se likhna padta tha
1980sMachine learning, classificationChhota data, chhote models
1990s–2000sNeural networks — CNN, RNN, GANBrain ko imitate karna shuru
2017Transformer — “Attention Is All You Need”Parallelism — training tez hui
2018–NowBade models, human demonstrationAI articles, news, code likhta hai

4. Try karo — time travel karo

Neeche steps me dekho har era me AI kya kar sakta tha.

  1. 1. 1950s
    [AI] Rule-based: 'Agar baarish ho to chhata lo'
    [Limit] Har rule haath se likhna padta hai
    [Result] Sirf bahut simple kaam
  2. 2. 1980s
    [AI] ML classification — chhote data par training
    [Kaam] Spam ya not-spam pehchanna
    [Limit] Data aur compute kam the
  3. 3. 1990s–2000s
    [CNN] Images pehchanna — cat ya dog?
    [RNN] Language samajhna — agla word kya hoga?
    [GAN] Nayi images banana — asli jaisi
  4. 4. 2017 + aaj
    [Transformer] Parallel training — hafton ka kaam dinon me
    [ChatGPT] Articles, news, code — sab likhta hai
    [Lesson] 70 saal ki research — ek din ka magic nahi

5. Eras — ek table me

EraModelKhaasiyat
1950sRule-basedHaath se likhe rules
1980sMachine LearningData se seekhna, classification
1990s–2000sCNN / RNN / GANImages, language, generation
2017TransformerAttention + parallelism
2018–NowLarge modelsMassive data + human demonstration

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. ChatGPT ko ‘achanak’ samajhna — 70 saal ki research hai peeche.
2. Transformer ko sirf ‘ek aur model’ samajhna — parallelism hi uska breakthrough tha.
3. CNN/RNN/GAN ko ek samajhna — CNN images, RNN language, GAN generation — alag kaam.
4. Rule-based ko bekaar samajhna — har era ne agle ki neev rakhi.
5. AI ko sirf ChatGPT samajhna — ChatGPT ek application hai, research bahut badi hai.

7. Interview corner

Q: “Transformer itna important kyun hai?”
A: Kyunki isne parallelism laaya — pehle ke models (RNN) sequence me ek ke baad ek chalte the, Transformer ek saath process karta hai. Isse training time hafton se dinon me aa gaya, aur bade models train karna possible hua.
Q: “CNN, RNN aur GAN me kya farak hai?”
A: CNN visual tasks (images) ke liye, RNN natural language tasks ke liye, GAN generative hai — do networks (generative + discriminative) se nayi, asli jaisi images/data banata hai.
Q: “ChatGPT achanak kaise aa gaya?”
A: Nahi aaya — 1950s rules, 1980s ML, 1990s NN, 2017 Transformer, phir 2018 ke baad bade models aur human demonstration se training. 70 saal ki research ka result hai.

8. Quick check

1. Transformer model kis paper se aaya?

  • ✓ ‘Attention Is All You Need’ (2017)
  • ‘Deep Learning’ (1980s)
  • ‘ChatGPT’ (2022)

2. Images pehchanne ke liye kaun sa neural network use hota hai?

  • ✓ CNN — Convolutional Neural Network
  • RNN
  • GAN
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: 1950s rules → 1980s ML → 1990s CNN/RNN/GAN → 2017 Transformer (attention + parallelism) → 2018 ke baad bade models. ChatGPT ek din ka magic nahi — 70 saal ki research ka phal hai.

04System Design 101 · S19 · Guide 4 / 8

DeepSeek 1-Pager

DeepSeek ne duniya ko hairan kar diya: powerful AI model, sirf ~$6 million me final training run, aur Jan 2025 me DeepSeek R1 release hote hi Apple App Store par No. 1 free app. Raaz hai GRPO — ek reinforcement learning technique. Is page me samjho.

1. DeepSeek — kam paise me bada model

Socho do halwai hain: ek ke paas 100 crore ka kitchen hai, dusre ke paas 6 lakh ka. Dusra halwai kehta hai — “main tumse behtar mithai bana loonga, kyunki mera tareeka alag hai.” DeepSeek wahi dusra halwai hai.

Zyada tar AI models supervised fine-tuning se train hote hain — insaan ke likhe hue examples ko copy kar ke. DeepSeek R1 ne reinforcement learning (GRPO) use kiya — model khud try karta hai, reward milta hai, aur behtar hota jata hai. Isliye reasoning me mazboot hai.

2. DeepSeek R1 ke 5 main points

Guide ke hisaab se — cost, GRPO, aur R1 kya alag karta hai.

Cost — sirf ~$6 million

DeepSeek R1 ki final training run ki cost lagbhag $6 million batayi jati hai — bade American models ke muqable bahut kam. Isi ne duniya ko hairan kar diya: itne kam paise me itna powerful model kaise?

Note: ye sirf final training run ki cost hai — research, experiments aur infrastructure alag hai. Lekin phir bhi, ye batata hai ki efficiency se cost bahut kam ho sakti hai.

R1 — January 2025 release

Jan 2025 me DeepSeek ne apna latest reasoning-focused model R1 release kiya. Release ke baad ye Apple App Store par No. 1 downloaded free app ban gaya.

Reasoning-focused ka matlab: model sirf jawab nahi deta, wo soch kar jawab deta hai — maths, coding aur logic wale sawaalon me behtar hai.

Supervised fine-tuning ki problem

Zyada tar models supervised fine-tuning (SFT) se train hote hain — insaan ke annotated examples ko dekh kar copy karna. Isme limit hai: model sirf utna hi seekh sakta hai jitna examples me hai, aur human annotation mehenga aur slow hota hai.

Isliye SFT se reasoning (sochna) achhe se nahi aata — model jawab yaad karta hai, sochna nahi seekhta.

GRPO — Group Relative Policy Optimization

DeepSeek R1 GRPO use karta hai — ek reinforcement learning technique. Isme model kai jawab generate karta hai, unhe ek dusre se compare karta hai, aur behtar jawab ko reward milta hai.

Isse model khud seekhta hai kaun sa reasoning behtar hai — bina har cheez ke liye human examples ke. Yehi wajah hai R1 reasoning me mazboot hai.

Interview line: “SFT = copy karna, RL (GRPO) = try kar ke seekhna. Reasoning ke liye try kar ke seekhna behtar hai.”

Asar — AI industry par

R1 ke release ne bataya: powerful AI banane ke liye hamesha sabse zyada paise aur sabse bade data center ki zaroorat nahi — efficiency aur naye training tareeke se bhi ho sakta hai.

Isse open-source aur chhoti teams ke liye raasta khula — aur badi companies ko apni cost par dobara sochna pada.

R1 ke facts — numbers jo interview me poochhe jate hain

  • Architecture: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) — kul 671 billion parameters, lekin har task par sirf 37 billion parameters activate hote hain. Isi selective activation se resource bachta hai.
  • Training data: 14.8 trillion tokens, 52 languages me pre-train hua.
  • GPUs: sirf 2000 Nvidia GPUs se train hua — muqable me ChatGPT-4 ko lagbhag 25,000 Nvidia GPUs chahiye the, 90–100 din tak.
  • Cost: competitors se 85–90% zyada cost-effective.
  • Strengths: mathematics, coding aur reasoning tasks me behtareen.
  • Open-source: MIT license ke under open-source release hua.

3. SFT vs GRPO — ek table me

CheezSupervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)GRPO (Reinforcement Learning)
Seekhne ka tareekaHuman examples ko copy karoKai jawab try karo, behtar ko reward do
DataHuman-annotated examples chahiye (mehenga)Reward signal se seekhta hai
ReasoningKamzor — jawab yaad karta haiMazboot — sochna seekhta hai
CostAnnotation mehenga aur slowKam human data chahiye
ExampleZyada tar traditional modelsDeepSeek R1

Numbers: ~$6M final training run, Jan 2025 R1 release, App Store No. 1 free app.

4. Try karo — ek maths problem, do tareeke se

Neeche steps me dekho SFT aur GRPO wala model ek hi problem kaise solve karta hai.

  1. 1. Problem aayi
    [User] Poochha: 'Ek train 60 km/h se 2.5 ghante chalti hai — kitni door jayegi?'
    [SFT Model] Yaad kiya: aise sawaal ka jawab '150 km' hota hai
    [GRPO Model] Socha: 60 × 2.5 = 150 km
  2. 2. SFT model ka jawab
    [SFT] Jawab: '150 km' — sahi hai, lekin agar sawaal thoda badla to?
    [SFT] Naya sawaal: 'Train 45 min rukti hai to?' — confuse ho gaya
    [Limit] Yaad kiya hua jawab — socha nahi
  3. 3. GRPO model ka jawab
    [GRPO] Kai tareeke try kiye: 60×2.5, 60×2 + 60×0.5...
    [GRPO] Best reasoning ko reward mila — jawab: 150 km
    [GRPO] Naya sawaal bhi solve kiya — kyunki sochna seekha hai
  4. 4. Result
    [R1] Reasoning-focused — maths aur coding me mazboot
    [Cost] ~$6M me train hua — efficiency ka example
    Lesson: copy karna nahi, sochna seekhna hai

5. DeepSeek R1 — ek table me

CheezDetailKyun important
Final training cost~$6 millionBade models se bahut kam
ReleaseJan 2025, R1Reasoning-focused model
App StoreNo. 1 free appAam logon tak pahuncha
TrainingGRPO (RL)Copy nahi, try kar ke seekhna
SFT ki limitHuman examplesMehenga, reasoning kamzor
Architecture (MoE)671B total, 37B active per taskSelective activation — resource bachta hai
Training data14.8 trillion tokens, 52 languagesBada aur diverse data
GPUs2000 Nvidia GPUs (ChatGPT-4: ~25K, 90–100 din)Kam hardware, kam cost
Cost-effectivenessCompetitors se 85–90% zyadaEfficiency ka saboot
LicenseMIT open-sourceKoi bhi use kar sakta hai

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. $6M ko poori cost samajhna — ye sirf final training run hai, research aur infra alag hai.
2. GRPO ko ‘magic’ samajhna — ye reinforcement learning hai, reward signal se seekhna.
3. SFT ko bekaar samajhna — SFT abhi bhi kaam aata hai; GRPO reasoning ke liye behtar hai.
4. Cost kam hone ka matlab quality kam samajhna — R1 reasoning me mazboot hai, cost efficiency se aayi hai.
5. DeepSeek ko sirf ‘cheap model’ kehna — asli kahani training technique (GRPO) ki hai.

7. Interview corner

Q: “GRPO kya hai?”
A: Group Relative Policy Optimization — ek reinforcement learning technique. Model kai jawab generate karta hai, unhe ek dusre se compare karta hai, aur behtar jawab ko reward milta hai. Isse model reasoning seekhta hai, bina har cheez ke human examples ke.
Q: “Supervised fine-tuning ki limit kya hai?”
A: Model sirf human-annotated examples ko copy karta hai — utna hi seekh sakta hai jitna examples me hai. Human annotation mehenga aur slow hota hai, aur reasoning (sochna) achhe se nahi aata.
Q: “DeepSeek R1 itna famous kyun hua?”
A: Kyunki isne ~$6 million me powerful reasoning model banaya aur Jan 2025 me release hote hi App Store par No. 1 free app ban gaya — isne bataya efficiency se bhi top AI ban sakta hai.

8. Quick check

1. DeepSeek R1 kis technique se train hua?

  • ✓ GRPO — reinforcement learning, kai jawab compare kar ke seekhna
  • Sirf supervised fine-tuning
  • Rule-based programming

2. DeepSeek R1 ki final training run ki cost kitni batayi jati hai?

  • ✓ Lagbhag $6 million
  • $6 billion
  • $600
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: ~$6M final training run, Jan 2025 me R1, App Store No. 1. Raaz GRPO hai — model copy nahi karta, kai jawab try kar ke behtar ko reward deta hai, isliye reasoning mazboot hai. Efficiency bhi ek innovation hai.

05System Design 101 · S19 · Guide 5 / 8

The Open Source AI Stack

AI app banane ke liye lakhon rupaye nahi chahiye — best AI tools open-source hain. Frontend se lekar LLM tak, har layer ka free aur powerful option hai: NextJS, LangChain, Ollama, Llama, Postgres, Milvus. Ye page poora open-source AI stack batata hai.

1. Open-source AI stack — apni dukaan kholo

AI app banana pehle sirf badi companies ka kaam tha — unke paas paise, data aur models the. Ab open-source tools se koi bhi apni AI dukaan khol sakta hai: UI free, model free, database free.

Stack ki har layer me options hain — tumhe sirf apne kaam ke hisaab se chunna hai. Ye page wahi menu hai.

2. Stack ki 5 paratein

Guide ke hisaab se — har layer me kaun se open-source tools hain.

Frontend — NextJS, Streamlit, Vercel

Beautiful AI UIs banane ke liye NextJS (React framework) aur Streamlit (Python se turant UI) best hain. Deployment ke liye Vercel hai.

Streamlit se data wale log bina frontend seekhe hi AI demo bana sakte hain — Python likho, UI ban gaya.

Embeddings aur RAG — Nomic, JinaAI, Cognito, LLMAware

Embedding models text ko numbers (vectors) me badalte hain — taaki similar cheezein dhoondh sakein. RAG libraries (Nomic, JinaAI, Cognito, LLMAware) se accurate search aur RAG features bante hain.

RAG ka matlab: model ko apne documents se jawab dhoondh kar dena — bina model ko dobara train kiye.

Backend aur Model Access — FastAPI, LangChain, Ollama, HuggingFace

Backend ke liye FastAPI (tez Python API), LangChain (LLM apps ka framework), aur Netflix Metaflow hain. Model access ke liye Ollama (local models chalao) aur HuggingFace (models ka hub) hain.

Ollama se Llama jaisa model apne laptop par chala sakte ho — bina cloud ke, bina paise ke.

Data aur Retrieval — Postgres, Milvus, Weaviate, PGVector, FAISS

Data store aur retrieval ke liye: Postgres (+ PGVector extension — vectors bhi store karo), Milvus aur Weaviate (vector databases), FAISS (fast similarity search library).

Vector DB ka kaam: “is document ke sabse similar documents kaun se hain?” — ye RAG ki neev hai.

LLMs — Llama, Mistral, Qwen, Phi, Gemma

Performance benchmarks ke hisaab se open-source models — Llama, Mistral, Qwen, Phi, Gemma — proprietary LLMs (GPT, Claude) ke great alternatives hain.

Inhe apne server par chala sakte ho — data bahar nahi jata, cost control me rehta hai, aur customization apne hisaab se kar sakte ho.

Interview line: “Open-source stack ka matlab: koi vendor lock-in nahi — har layer badli ja sakti hai.”

3. Poora stack — ek table me

LayerToolsKaam
FrontendNextJS, Streamlit, VercelAI UI + deployment
Embeddings / RAGNomic, JinaAI, Cognito, LLMAwareAccurate search + RAG
BackendFastAPI, LangChain, MetaflowAPI + LLM app logic
Model AccessOllama, HuggingFaceModels chalao / dhoondho
Data / RetrievalPostgres, Milvus, Weaviate, PGVector, FAISSVectors store + similar search
LLMsLlama, Mistral, Qwen, Phi, GemmaOpen models — GPT/Claude ke alternatives

4. Try karo — apni AI app banao

Neeche steps me dekho open-source stack se ek AI app kaise banti hai.

  1. 1. UI banao
    [Streamlit] Python me 20 lines — chatbot UI taiyaar
    [Vercel] Deploy kiya — link mil gaya
    [Result] UI ready — bina frontend seekhe
  2. 2. Documents daalo
    [Embeddings] Nomic se documents ke vectors banaye
    [Milvus] Vectors store kiye — similar search ke liye
    [RAG] Sawal aate hi relevant documents niklenge
  3. 3. Model chuno
    [Ollama] Llama model apne laptop par chalaya
    [LangChain] RAG chain banayi — docs + model jode
    [FastAPI] Backend API banayi — UI se jodi
  4. 4. App live!
    [User] Poochha: 'Refund policy kya hai?'
    [RAG] Relevant docs mile → Llama ne jawab banaya
    [Cost] ₹0 — sab open-source, apne machine par

5. Har layer, ek line me

LayerToolsYaad rakhne wali baat
FrontendNextJS, StreamlitStreamlit se Python me hi UI
Embeddings/RAGNomic, JinaAIText → vectors, phir search
BackendFastAPI, LangChainAPI + LLM logic
Model AccessOllama, HuggingFaceLocal models chalao
DataPostgres + PGVector, MilvusVectors store karo
LLMsLlama, Mistral, Qwen, Phi, GemmaOpen models — data bahar nahi jata

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Har layer me proprietary tool chunna — open-source se shuru karo, zaroorat ho to upgrade karo.
2. RAG ke bina seedha model se poochhna — model ko tumhare documents ka pata nahi; RAG se pehle relevant docs do.
3. Vector DB ke bina RAG banana — similar documents dhoondhne ke liye vector search chahiye.
4. Ollama ko ‘sirf demo’ samajhna — local models production me bhi chalte hain, privacy ke liye best hain.
5. Ek hi LLM par depend rehna — stack ki har layer badli ja sakti hai; vendor lock-in se bacho.

7. Interview corner

Q: “RAG kya hai?”
A: Retrieval-Augmented Generation — model ko jawab dene se pehle apne documents se relevant information dhoondh kar di jati hai. Isse model tumhare data par sahi jawab deta hai, bina dobara train kiye. Iske liye embeddings aur vector DB chahiye.
Q: “Open-source LLM ke fayde kya hain?”
A: Data bahar nahi jata (privacy), cost control me rehta hai, customization apne hisaab se kar sakte ho, aur vendor lock-in nahi hota. Llama, Mistral, Qwen, Phi, Gemma — benchmarks me proprietary models ke kareeb hain.
Q: “Ollama kya karta hai?”
A: Ollama se open-source LLMs (jaise Llama) ko apne laptop/server par aasani se chala sakte ho — bina cloud ke. Isse local AI apps banti hain.

8. Quick check

1. RAG me documents dhoondhne ke liye kya use hota hai?

  • ✓ Embeddings + Vector DB (jaise Milvus, PGVector) — similar documents search
  • Sirf SQL
  • Sirf frontend

2. Apne laptop par Llama jaisa model chalane ke liye kya use karte hain?

  • ✓ Ollama
  • Streamlit
  • FastAPI
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Frontend NextJS/Streamlit, RAG Nomic/JinaAI, backend FastAPI/LangChain, model access Ollama/HuggingFace, data Postgres/Milvus/PGVector, LLMs Llama/Mistral/Qwen/Phi/Gemma. Paisa nahi, stack chahiye — AI app ab koi bhi bana sakta hai.

← Previous04 · DeepSeek 1-PagerNext →06 · What is an AI Agent?
06System Design 101 · S19 · Guide 6 / 8

What is an AI Agent?

AI agent ek aisa software program hai jo khud soch kar kaam karta hai — environment ko samajhta hai, data ikattha karta hai, tools use karta hai, aur apne goal tak pahunchne ke liye best action chunta hai. Chatbot se aage — agent kaam karta hai, sirf jawab nahi deta.

1. AI agent — ek smart naukar wali kahani

Ek naukar ko kaho “chai banao” — wo khud jaanta hai: paani kahan hai, doodh kahan hai, gas kaise jalani hai, aur chai ban ke tumhe de deta hai. Tumhe har step batane ki zaroorat nahi.

AI agent wahi naukar hai: tum goal dete ho (“meri flight book karo”), agent khud perceive karta hai (flight search karta hai), tools use karta hai (booking API), memory se tumhari pasand yaad rakhta hai, aur kaam kar ke deta hai. Chatbot sirf bolta hai — agent karta hai.

2. Agent ki 5 khaasiyat

Guide ke hisaab se — ek agent me kya-kya hota hai.

Autonomous actions — human-in-the-loop ke saath

Agent khud actions le sakta hai — bina har baar insaan se poochhe. Lekin control ke liye human-in-the-loop bhi ho sakta hai — important action se pehle insaan se approval le lo.

Example: agent flight dhoondh le, lekin book karne se pehle tumse poochhe — “ye wali book kar doon?” Yehi sahi balance hai.

Memory — pasand aur knowledge yaad rakhta hai

Agent ke paas memory hoti hai — tumhari preferences (window seat pasand hai), aur knowledge (pehle ki bookings). Isse personalization milta hai — har baar sab kuch dobara batane ki zaroorat nahi.

Memory ke bina agent har baar naya hota — tumhe har baar sab kuch dobara batana padta.

LLM — information processing aur decisions

LLM (Large Language Model) agent ka dimaag hai — information process karta hai aur decisions leta hai: aage kya karna hai, kaun sa tool use karna hai.

LLM bina agent sirf text generate karta hai; agent me LLM ke saath tools, memory aur goals judte hain — tab wo kaam kar pata hai.

Perception aur Tools — duniya se judna

Agent ko apne environment ko perceive karna padta hai — kya ho raha hai, kya badla hai. Aur phir tools use karta hai: internet access, code interpreter, API calls.

Example: agent ko pata chale flight delay hui (perceive), to wo hotel API se naya hotel book kare (tool use).

Collaboration aur Agent ke types

Agents dusre agents ya humans ke saath collaborate kar sakte hain. Types: learning agents, simple reflex agents, model-based reflex agents, goal-based agents, utility-based agents — har type alag tareeke se decide karta hai.

Architectures: Single Agent (personal assistant), Multi-Agent (agents ek dusre se collaborate ya compete karein), Human-Machine (insaan ke saath mil kar kaam karein).

Interview line: “Chatbot jawab deta hai, agent kaam karta hai — farak tools, memory aur goals ka hai.”

3. Agent = LLM + Tools + Memory + Goals

AI Agent ke 4 pillars:
  1. LLM (dimaag) — soche, decide kare
  2. Tools — internet, code, APIs se kaam kare
  3. Memory — pasand aur knowledge yaad rakhe
  4. Goals — khud best action chune

Architectures:
  Single Agent   → personal assistant
  Multi-Agent    → kai agents collaborate/competite karein
  Human-Machine  → insaan ke saath mil kar kaam

Agent types: learning, simple reflex, model-based reflex,
goal-based, utility-based

4. Try karo — ek agent se flight book karwao

Neeche steps me dekho AI agent tumhara kaam kaise karta hai.

  1. 1. Goal do
    [You] 'Mujhe Delhi se Mumbai ki subah ki flight book karo'
    [Agent] Goal samjha: flight book karni hai, subah ki, Delhi → Mumbai
    [Memory] Tumhe window seat pasand hai — yaad hai
  2. 2. Perceive + Tools
    [Tool] Flight search API — 6 flights mili
    [LLM] Best chuni: 7 AM, ₹4,200, window seat available
    [Human-in-loop] 'Ye wali book kar doon? ₹4,200' — tumne Haan kaha
  3. 3. Kaam karo
    [Tool] Booking API se ticket book hua — PNR ABC123
    [Memory] Ye booking save hui — agli baar kaam aayegi
    [You] Ticket mil gaya — tumne sirf ek line boli thi
  4. 4. Chatbot se farak
    [Chatbot] Sirf batata: 'Flights ye hain...'
    [Agent] Kaam karta: search + book + yaad rakhta
    Farak: tools + memory + goals

5. Agent ke hisse — ek table me

HissaKaamNa ho to kya hoga
LLM (dimaag)Sochna, decide karnaAgent kuch decide nahi kar payega
ToolsInternet, code, APIsAgent sirf bol payega, kar nahi payega
MemoryPasand + knowledgeHar baar sab kuch dobara batana padega
GoalsBest action chunnaAgent ko pata nahi hoga kya karna hai
Human-in-loopImportant action se pehle approvalGalat booking ho sakti hai

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Chatbot ko agent samajhna — bina tools aur memory ke wo sirf chatbot hai.
2. Human-in-loop na rakhna — agent paise kharch kar de ya galat booking kar de.
3. Memory na banana — har baar user ko sab kuch dobara batana padega.
4. Har kaam ke liye ek bada agent banana — chhote agents, har ek ka ek kaam, phir multi-agent se jodo.
5. Tools ko bina permission ke chalana — agent ko sirf wahi tools do jo use chahiye, aur sensitive actions par approval lo.

7. Interview corner

Q: “AI agent aur chatbot me kya farak hai?”
A: Chatbot sirf jawab deta hai. Agent ke paas tools (APIs, internet), memory (preferences) aur goals hote hain — wo khud actions le kar kaam karta hai, jaise flight book karna.
Q: “Human-in-the-loop kyun zaroori hai?”
A: Agent autonomous hai, lekin paise ya important decisions wale actions se pehle insaan ki approval chahiye — nahi to galat booking ya galat payment ho sakta hai. Control insaan ke paas rehna chahiye.
Q: “Multi-agent architecture kya hai?”
A: Kai agents ek saath kaam karte hain — collaborate ya compete kar ke. Jaise ek agent flight dhoondhe, dusra hotel, teesra dono ko combine kare. Har agent ka apna kaam hota hai.

8. Quick check

1. AI agent chatbot se alag kaise hota hai?

  • ✓ Agent ke paas tools, memory aur goals hote hain — wo kaam karta hai, sirf jawab nahi deta
  • Agent zyada bolta hai
  • Koi farak nahi hai

2. Agent ka ‘dimaag’ kya hota hai?

  • ✓ LLM — information process karta hai aur decisions leta hai
  • Database
  • Frontend
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Agent = LLM (dimaag) + Tools (kaam) + Memory (yaad) + Goals (maksad). Chatbot bolta hai, agent karta hai — aur important kaam se pehle human-in-the-loop rakho. Architectures: Single, Multi-Agent, Human-Machine.
SOURCESource: https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/what-is-an-ai-agent.md
← Previous05 · The Open Source AI StackNext →07 · Data Pipelines Overview
07System Design 101 · S19 · Guide 7 / 8

Data Pipelines Overview

Data pipeline wo rasta hai jis se data source se lekar dashboard tak pahunchta hai — 5 phases: Collect, Ingest, Store, Compute, Consume. Har phase ka apna kaam hai, aur koi ek phase kharab ho to poora data galat ho jayega. Samjho poora flow.

1. Data pipeline — paani ki pipeline wali kahani

Paani nadi se aata hai, tanki me jama hota hai, filter hota hai, aur phir nal se ghar tak pahunchta hai. Agar filter kharab ho to ganda paani aayega — chahe nadi saaf ho.

Data pipeline wahi hai: data collect karo (nadi), ingest karo (tanki), store karo (bada tank), compute karo (filter + saaf karo), aur consume karo (nal se piyo — dashboard, ML, apps).

2. 5 phases — ek-ek karke

Guide ke hisaab se — data pipelines ke 5 predominant phases.

Phase 1 — Collect (ikattha karo)

Data data stores, data streams aur applications se aata hai — devices, apps, business systems se, remote sources se. Ye sabse pehla step hai: data kahan se aayega?

Example: website clicks, mobile app events, IoT sensors, payment systems — sab alag-alag sources hain.

Phase 2 — Ingest (andar lao)

Ingestion me data ko systems me load kiya jata hai aur event queues me organize kiya jata hai. Data aate hi use sahi jagah par lagana — queue me daalna taaki aage ka kaam order se ho.

Batch vs Stream: batch me data ek saath aata hai (raat ko), stream me lagatar aata hai (har second). Dono ke ingestion alag hote hain.

Phase 3 — Store (rakho)

Ingestion ke baad data data warehouses, data lakes aur lakehouses me store hota hai — saath me databases aur alag systems bhi. Store karna isliye kyunki compute baad me hota hai, aur data ko kahin to rakhna hai.

Yaad rakho: lake raw data ke liye, warehouse structured ke liye (Page 84).

Phase 4 — Compute (saaf + process karo)

Data par aggregation, cleansing aur manipulation hoti hai — company standards ke hisaab se: format conversion, compression, partitioning. Batch aur stream processing dono use hote hain.

Yehi “filter” hai — ganda data yahan saaf hota hai. Agar compute galat ho to dashboard galat dikhega, chahe data sahi ho.

Phase 5 — Consume (use karo)

Processed data consume hota hai: analytics aur visualization tools, operational data stores, decision engines, user-facing applications, dashboards, data science, ML (machine learning) services, BI (business intelligence) aur self-service analytics se.

Ye aakhri phase hai — data ka matlab tabhi hai jab koi use kare: dashboard dekhe, model train kare, ya decision le.

Interview line: “Pipeline ki har phase ki efficiency poori data-driven operation ki success decide karti hai.”

3. Poora flow — ek nazar me

Sources (devices, apps, streams, stores)
  → COLLECT: data ikattha karo
  → INGEST: load karo, event queues me organize karo
  → STORE: warehouse / lake / lakehouse me rakho
  → COMPUTE: aggregate, cleanse, transform (batch + stream)
  → CONSUME: dashboards, ML, BI, apps, decision engines
PhaseKaamTools (examples)
CollectSources se data laoAPIs, SDKs, Kafka
IngestLoad + queues me organizeKafka, Kinesis
StoreWarehouse / Lake / LakehouseSnowflake, S3, Databricks
ComputeClean, aggregate, transformSpark, Flink
ConsumeDashboards, ML, BITableau, ML services

4. Try karo — ek click ki journey

Neeche steps me dekho ek click pipeline ke 5 phases se kaise guzarta hai.

  1. 1. Collect
    [User] Website par 'Buy' dabaya
    [Collect] Click event — device, app, web se aaya
    [Sources] Clicks + payments + logs — sab ikatthe hue
  2. 2. Ingest
    [Kafka] Event queue me gaya — order se
    [Ingest] Data load hua — stream me, har second
    [Queue] Aage ka kaam queue se hoga — kuch khoyega nahi
  3. 3. Store
    [Lake] Raw event S3 me gaya
    [Warehouse] Structured copy Snowflake me
    [Store] Data safe hai — compute baad me hoga
  4. 4. Compute
    [Spark] Batch: aaj ki sales aggregate hui
    [Flink] Stream: abhi kitne log khareed rahe hain
    [Clean] Galat entries hatayi, format convert kiya
  5. 5. Consume
    [Dashboard] 'Aaj ki sales: ₹12 lakh' — Tableau par
    [ML] Recommendation model ko naya data mila
    [Decision] Team ne dekha: ye product zyada bik raha hai — stock badhao

5. 5 phases — ek table me

PhaseKaamGalti ho to kya hoga
CollectSources se data laoSource chhoota to data hi nahi aayega
IngestLoad + queuesBina queue ke spike me data kho jayega
StoreWarehouse/Lake me rakhoGalat store se cost ya speed bigdegi
ComputeClean + aggregateGanda data = galat dashboard
ConsumeDashboards, ML, BIData ka koi use nahi to pipeline bekaar

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Compute ke bina seedha consume karna — ganda data dashboard par galat dikhega.
2. Ingest me queue na rakhna — traffic spike aate hi data kho jayega.
3. Har data ko warehouse me daalna — raw data lake me, structured warehouse me.
4. Pipeline ki monitoring na karna — ek phase fail ho to pata hi nahi chalega kahan ruka.
5. Batch aur stream ko ek samajhna — batch raat ko, stream har second; dono ke tools aur design alag hain.

7. Interview corner

Q: “Data pipeline ke 5 phases kya hain?”
A: Collect, Ingest, Store, Compute, Consume. Collect: sources se data lao. Ingest: load karke queues me organize karo. Store: warehouse/lake me rakho. Compute: clean, aggregate, transform karo. Consume: dashboards, ML, BI se use karo.
Q: “Batch aur stream processing me kya farak hai?”
A: Batch me data ek saath process hota hai (jaise raat ko poora din ka data). Stream me data aate hi process hota hai (har second). Real-time chahiye to stream, cost kam chahiye to batch.
Q: “Pipeline me queue kyun chahiye?”
A: Taaki spike aane par data khoye nahi — producer queue me daale, consumer apni speed se le. Bina queue ke slow consumer se data loss hoga.

8. Quick check

1. Data pipeline ka pehla phase kaun sa hai?

  • ✓ Collect — sources se data ikattha karna
  • Consume
  • Compute

2. Data saaf aur aggregate kis phase me hota hai?

  • ✓ Compute phase me
  • Collect phase me
  • Store phase me
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Collect → Ingest → Store → Compute → Consume. Data nadi se nal tak: ikattha karo, queue me lao, store karo, saaf karo, phir dashboard/ML se use karo. Ek phase kharab ho to poora data galat.
SOURCESource: https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/data-pipelines-overview.md

08System Design 101 · S19 · Guide 8 / 8

How does ChatGPT work?

ChatGPT kaise kaam karta hai? Do hisse hain: Training (pre-training + fine-tuning) aur Inference (tumhare sawaal ka jawab). OpenAI ne saari details nahi di hain — isliye kuch hisse approximate hain — lekin basic flow samajhna interview ke liye kaafi hai.

1. ChatGPT — ek student wali kahani

Ek student pehle saari kitabein padhta hai (pre-training) — use duniya ka gyaan milta hai, lekin wo exam ke hisaab se jawab nahi de sakta. Phir teacher use exam ke examples se train karta hai (fine-tuning) — ab wo sawaal ke hisaab se jawab deta hai. Phir exam me baithta hai (inference) — ek-ek word soch kar jawab likhta hai.

ChatGPT wahi student hai: internet ka data padh kar (pre-training), human feedback se seekh kar (fine-tuning), aur phir tumhare sawaal ka jawab ek-ek token bana kar deta hai.

2. Kaam karne ke 5 hisse

Guide ke hisaab se — training ke 2 stages aur inference ka flow. (Note: OpenAI ne saari details share nahi ki hain, isliye kuch hisse approximate hain.)

Pre-training — internet padhna

Pehle stage me GPT model (decoder-only Transformer) ko internet ke bade hisse par train kiya jata hai. Objective simple hai: agle word ko predict karo — sentence dekh kar aage kya aayega, ye seekhna.

Isse model ko grammar, facts aur language ka sense milta hai. Lekin pre-training ke baad model sirf sentence complete kar sakta hai — sawaal ka jawab dena nahi jaanta. Jaise “Paris is the capital of” → “France” — complete kar dega, lekin baat-cheet nahi karega.

Fine-tuning — insaan se seekhna

Dusre stage me model ko human feedback se train karte hain (RLHF — Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback). Insaan model ke jawab ko rank karta hai — kaun sa jawab behtar hai — aur model us hisaab se seekhta hai.

Isse model helpful, safe aur sawaal ke hisaab se jawab dena seekhta hai. Yehi stage ChatGPT ko “chatbot” banati hai — warna wo sirf sentence completer rehta.

Fine-tuning ke 3 steps (original guide se)

  1. Step 1 — SFT data: training data (sawaal aur jawab) ikattha karo, aur pre-trained model ko is data par fine-tune karo. Model sawaal input le kar training data jaisa jawab generate karna seekhta hai.
  2. Step 2 — Reward model: aur data ikattha karo (ek sawaal, kai jawab) aur ek reward model train karo jo jawabon ko sabse relevant se least relevant tak rank kare.
  3. Step 3 — RL with PPO: reinforcement learning (PPO optimization) se model ko fine-tune karo, taaki uske jawab aur accurate ho jayein.

Tokens — words ke tukde

Model words ko nahi, tokens ko samajhta hai — words ke chhote tukde. “ChatGPT” 2 tokens ho sakta hai, “unbelievable” 3-4. Har token ek number hota hai, aur model numbers par kaam karta hai.

Kyun important hai? Context window tokens me hoti hai (jaise 128k tokens) — tum kitna lamba conversation kar sakte ho, ye tokens se decide hota hai. Aur cost bhi tokens se hoti hai.

Inference — ek-ek token bana kar

Jab tum sawaal bhejte ho, to model ek-ek token predict karta hai — pehla token, phir use dekh kar dusra, phir teesra. Aise hi poora jawab banta hai. Isiliye ChatGPT ka jawab dheere-dheere type hota dikhta hai.

Temperature control karta hai randomness: low temperature = safe, predictable jawab; high temperature = creative, alag jawab.

Interview line: “ChatGPT likhta nahi, predict karta hai — ek token ke baad agla token, baar-baar.”

Sawaal ka jawab — 7 steps (original guide se)

Example sawaal: “Explain how a classification algorithm works”.

  1. Step 1: user poora sawaal likhta hai.
  2. Step 2: sawaal content moderation component ko jata hai — ye check karta hai ki sawaal safety guidelines violate to nahi karta, aur galat sawaalon ko filter karta hai.
  3. Step 3–4: agar sawaal moderation pass kar le to ChatGPT model ko jata hai; pass na kare to seedha template response generation me jata hai.
  4. Step 5–6: model jawab generate karta hai, phir jawab dobara content moderation se guzarta hai — taaki jawab safe, harmless aur unbiased ho.
  5. Step 7: agar jawab moderation pass kare to user ko dikhaya jata hai; pass na kare to template response banta hai aur user ko template jawab dikhta hai.

Limitations — kya nahi kar sakta

Model hallucinate kar sakta hai — galat jawab confident se de sakta hai, kyunki wo predict karta hai, “jaanta” nahi. Uska knowledge training data tak limited hai — nayi khabar nahi jaanta, bina browsing ke.

Isliye critical kaam (medical, legal, payments) me ChatGPT ka jawab verify karna chahiye — aur RAG (Page 87) se use apne documents se jodna chahiye.

3. Training vs Inference — ek table me

StageKya hota haiObjective
Pre-trainingInternet data par GPT (decoder-only Transformer) trainAgla word predict karo
Fine-tuning (RLHF)Human feedback se trainHelpful, safe, sawaal ke hisaab se jawab
InferenceTumhara prompt → ek-ek token generateJawab banao, token by token
Training:
  Internet text → Pre-training (next-word prediction)
    → Fine-tuning (RLHF: human ranks answers)
Inference:
  Tumhara prompt → Tokenize → Model predicts next token
    → Token by token → Poora jawab
  (Temperature: low = safe, high = creative)

Note: OpenAI ne saari details share nahi ki hain — isliye diagram ke kuch hisse approximate ho sakte hain.

4. Try karo — ek sawaal ka jawab banta hai

Neeche steps me dekho tumhare sawaal ka jawab token by token kaise banta hai.

  1. 1. Prompt bhejo
    [You] 'Paris kis desh ki rajdhani hai?'
    [Tokenize] Prompt tokens me toota: ['Paris', ' kis', ' desh', ...]
    [Model] Context taiyaar — ab agla token predict karega
  2. 2. Token by token
    [Token 1] 'France' — probability 0.98
    [Token 2] ' ki' — probability 0.95
    [Token 3] ' rajdhani' — probability 0.97
    [Token 4] ' hai' — probability 0.99
  3. 3. Jawab taiyaar
    [Output] 'France ki rajdhani hai.'
    [Temperature] Low thi — isliye safe aur predictable jawab
    [Note] Model ne 'jaana' nahi — predict kiya, training data se
  4. 4. Hallucination ka khatra
    [Sawaal] 'Mere gaon ke sarpanch ka naam kya hai?'
    [Model] Confident se ek naam bata dega — galat bhi ho sakta hai
    [Lesson] Critical sawaal par hamesha verify karo

5. Terms — ek table me

TermMatlabYaad rakhne wali baat
Pre-trainingInternet par next-word predictionModel ko language aur facts milte hain
Fine-tuning (RLHF)Human feedback se trainingChatbot banta hai — helpful + safe
TokenWord ka chhota tukdaContext aur cost tokens me hoti hai
InferencePrompt se token-by-token jawabJawab type hota dikhta hai
TemperatureRandomness controlLow = safe, High = creative
HallucinationGalat jawab confident seVerify karo — khaas taur par critical kaam me

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. ChatGPT ko ‘jaanne wala’ samajhna — wo predict karta hai, jaanta nahi; galat bhi ho sakta hai.
2. Pre-training aur fine-tuning ko ek samajhna — pre-training se language, fine-tuning se chatbot banta hai.
3. Temperature ko ignore karna — creative kaam me high, factual me low temperature chahiye.
4. Hallucination ko ignore karna — critical sawaal (medical, legal) me jawab verify karo.
5. Context window ko unlimited samajhna — lamba conversation tokens khata hai; purani baatein bhool sakta hai.

7. Interview corner

Q: “ChatGPT kaise train hota hai?”
A: Do stages: pre-training — GPT (decoder-only Transformer) ko internet data par train karte hain, objective agla word predict karna. Phir fine-tuning (RLHF) — human feedback se model helpful aur safe jawab dena seekhta hai.
Q: “ChatGPT jawab kaise generate karta hai?”
A: Token by token — pehla token predict karta hai, phir use dekh kar dusra, aise hi poora jawab banta hai. Isiliye jawab dheere-dheere type hota dikhta hai.
Q: “Hallucination kya hai?”
A: Jab model galat jawab confident se de — kyunki wo predict karta hai, ‘jaanta’ nahi. Isliye critical kaam me jawab verify karna chahiye, ya RAG se model ko apne documents se jodna chahiye.

8. Quick check

1. Pre-training me model kya seekhta hai?

  • ✓ Agla word predict karna — internet data par
  • Chat karna
  • Images banana

2. Fine-tuning (RLHF) se model kya seekhta hai?

  • ✓ Human feedback se helpful aur safe jawab dena
  • Tez type karna
  • Internet browse karna
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Pre-training (internet par next-word prediction) → Fine-tuning (RLHF — human feedback) → Inference (token by token jawab). Model jaanta nahi, predict karta hai — isliye hallucination hota hai aur verify karna zaroori hai.

F112 interview FAQs

FAQs — interview sawaal

Har sawaal par click karo — jawaab khul jayega. Ye sawaal interview me aksar poochhe jaate hain.

AI agent aur chatbot me kya farak hai?
Chatbot sirf jawab deta hai — sawaal suno, text me jawab do. AI agent kaam karta hai: uske paas tools (APIs, internet, code interpreter), memory (tumhari pasand aur pehle ka data) aur goals hote hain. Agent khud decide karta hai kaun sa action lena hai — jaise flight search karna, best wali chunna, aur booking API se ticket book karna. Chatbot bolta hai, agent karta hai. Aur important kaam se pehle agent human-in-the-loop rakhta hai — jaise book karne se pehle tumse poochhega.
LLM kya hota hai aur ye kaam kaise karta hai?
LLM (Large Language Model) ek bada neural network hai jo internet ke bade hisse par train hota hai. Ye words ko nahi, tokens ko samajhta hai — words ke chhote tukde. Training ke do stages hain: pre-training, jisme model agla word predict karna seekhta hai (decoder-only Transformer), aur fine-tuning (RLHF), jisme human feedback se model helpful aur safe jawab dena seekhta hai. Inference me model ek-ek token predict kar ke jawab banata hai — isiliye ChatGPT ka jawab dheere-dheere type hota dikhta hai.
RAG kya hai aur embeddings kaise kaam karte hain?
RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) ka matlab hai: model ko jawab dene se pehle tumhare documents se relevant information dhoondh kar de do. Embeddings text ko numbers (vectors) me badal dete hain — milte-julte matlab wale text ke vectors paas hote hain. Open-source stack me Nomic, JinaAI jaise embedding models aur Milvus, Weaviate, PGVector, FAISS jaise vector stores use hote hain. Isse model hallucinate kam karta hai, kyunki jawab tumhare data se aata hai, sirf training memory se nahi.
Pre-training aur fine-tuning me kya farak hai? RLHF kya hai?
Pre-training pehla stage hai: GPT model (decoder-only Transformer) ko internet data par train karte hain, objective agla word predict karna. Iske baad model sentence complete kar sakta hai, lekin sawaal ka jawab dena nahi jaanta. Fine-tuning dusra stage hai — 3 steps: (1) sawaal-jawab data par SFT, (2) kai jawabon ko rank kar ke reward model train karna, (3) PPO reinforcement learning se fine-tune karna. RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) me insaan jawabon ko rank karta hai aur model us hisaab se seekhta hai — isse model helpful aur safe banta hai.
DeepSeek R1 itna famous kyun hua? GRPO kya hai?
DeepSeek R1 ne sirf lagbhag $6 million ki final training run me powerful reasoning model banaya aur January 2025 me release hote hi Apple App Store par No. 1 free app ban gaya. Raaz hai GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization) — ek reinforcement learning technique jisme model kai jawab generate karta hai, unhe ek dusre se compare karta hai, aur behtar jawab ko reward milta hai. R1 Mixture-of-Experts architecture use karta hai: kul 671 billion parameters, lekin har task par sirf 37 billion activate hote hain. Sirf 2000 Nvidia GPUs lage (ChatGPT-4 ko ~25,000 lage the), aur ye competitors se 85–90% zyada cost-effective hai.
Data lake, data warehouse aur lakehouse me kya farak hai?
Data Lake raw, unstructured data ka pool hai — data native format me store hota hai, schema-on-read (padhte waqt structure lagta hai). Tools: S3, ADLS. Data Warehouse bada, structured repository hai — data aane se pehle clean aur organize hota hai (schema-on-write), complex queries aur historical analysis ke liye. Tools: Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift. Data Lakehouse dono ka mix hai — lake ki flexibility + warehouse ki reliability (Delta Lake lake par ACID transactions lata hai). Data Mart warehouse ka department-specific chhota hissa hai. Data Mesh in sab se alag hai — ye technology nahi, organizational approach hai: data ki ownership domain teams ke paas hoti hai.
Data pipeline ke 5 phases kya hain? Batch aur stream me kya farak hai?
5 phases hain: Collect (sources — devices, apps, streams — se data ikattha karo), Ingest (data load karo aur event queues me organize karo), Store (warehouse, lake ya lakehouse me rakho), Compute (aggregation, cleansing, format conversion, compression, partitioning — batch aur stream dono), Consume (dashboards, ML services, BI, decision engines se use karo). Batch me data ek saath process hota hai (jaise raat ko poora din ka data), stream me data aate hi process hota hai (har second). Real-time chahiye to stream, cost kam chahiye to batch. Ingest me queue isliye chahiye taaki traffic spike me data khoye nahi.
Pandas me merge, join, concat aur combine kab use karein?
Concat — do tables ko vertical ya horizontal jodna ho, jaise alag shards ka data ek saath karna. Append — existing table me naye rows add karne ho, jaise crawler ka naya data. Merge — alag domains ka data same key par jodna ho, SQL join jaisa (pd.merge(users, orders, on='user_id')). Join — index hi key ho (jaise time-series) to index par outer join. Combine — do tables jodte waqt calculation karni ho, jaise dono me same cell ho to chhoti value chunni ho (df1.combine(df2, np.minimum)) — data cleansing me kaam aata hai.
ChatGPT hallucinate kyun karta hai? Isse kaise bachein?
ChatGPT 'jaanta' nahi, predict karta hai — agla token kya aayega, ye probability se chunta hai. Isliye wo galat jawab bhi confident se de sakta hai — yehi hallucination hai. Uska knowledge training data tak limited hai — nayi khabar nahi jaanta, bina browsing ke. Temperature bhi matter karta hai: low temperature safe aur predictable jawab deta hai, high temperature creative lekin galat hone ka risk zyada. Bachne ke liye: critical kaam (medical, legal, payments) me jawab verify karo, aur RAG se model ko apne documents se jodo — jawab tumhare data se aayega, sirf prediction se nahi.
AI agent ki 5 khaasiyat kya hain?
Guide ke hisaab se 5 khaasiyat hain: (1) Autonomous actions — bina har baar insaan se poochhe khud action le sakta hai, lekin control ke liye human-in-the-loop rakhta hai. (2) Memory — tumhari preferences aur knowledge yaad rakhta hai, isse personalization milta hai. (3) LLM — information process karta hai aur decisions leta hai. (4) Perception aur Tools — environment ko perceive karta hai aur tools use karta hai (internet, code interpreter, API calls). (5) Collaboration — dusre agents ya humans ke saath mil kar kaam kar sakta hai. Agent ke types hain: learning, simple reflex, model-based reflex, goal-based aur utility-based.
Open-source AI stack se apni AI app kaise banayein?
Poora stack 5 paraton me banta hai: Frontend — NextJS ya Streamlit se UI banao, Vercel se deploy karo. Embeddings aur RAG — Nomic, JinaAI, Cognito ya LLMAware se accurate search aur RAG features. Backend aur Model Access — FastAPI ya LangChain se backend, Ollama ya HuggingFace se model access. Data aur Retrieval — Postgres, Milvus, Weaviate, PGVector ya FAISS se data store aur retrieval. LLMs — Llama, Mistral, Qwen, Phi ya Gemma — benchmarks ke hisaab se ye proprietary models (GPT, Claude) ke great alternatives hain. Paise kharch kiye bina poori AI app ban sakti hai.
System design interview me AI/ML system (jaise ChatGPT ya recommendation) kaise design karein?
Pehle requirements aur scale nikalo: kitne users, kitne requests per second, latency target kya hai. Phir high-level design banao: client → API gateway / load balancer → model serving layer (GPU inference servers) → cache (prompt cache, response cache) → data layer (vector DB for RAG, feature store, training data lake). Training aur inference ko alag rakho — training batch/offline hoti hai, inference real-time. Bottlenecks batao: GPU cost, token throughput, context window, hallucination. Trade-offs discuss karo: RAG vs fine-tuning, streaming vs batch inference, cost vs latency. Numbers se estimate karo — jaise QPS, tokens per second, GPU count — aur batayo scale kaise karoge (model replicas, sharding, caching).
